_shortName:
⛔ SHORT FORM — RULE REWRITTEN AFTER TESTING IT ON THE REAL 66. My first rule was 'part before the comma, else last two words', which produced 'Morvane of the' — IT CUT MID-PHRASE. ⚠️ THE NAMES COME IN THREE SHAPES: 9 with a comma, 18 beginning 'The', 3 plain.
   1. IF THERE IS A COMMA, take everything before it. 'Neth, Who Has Buried…' → 'Neth'.
   2. ELSE IF IT BEGINS 'The', take up to and including the first noun — stop BEFORE 'of', 'who', 'that'. 'The Hollow King of the Wild Half' → 'The Hollow King'. 'The Last Walker of the Sealed Wood' → 'The Last Walker'.
   3. ELSE take up to the first 'of'/'who'/'that'. 'Morvane of the Harvest Hand' → 'Morvane'. 'Vessa Who Trades in True Names' → 'Vessa'.
   4. IF THE RESULT IS UNDER 4 CHARACTERS OR EQUALS THE FULL NAME, USE THE FULL NAME. Some names do not shorten — 'The Raw Chord', 'The Starless One' — and that is fine.
⛔ NEVER CUT ON A PREPOSITION OR AN ARTICLE. 'Morvane of the' is the whole class of bug.
_whyItIsNews:
⛔ THE FIELD THAT MAKES A FIGHT NEWS IS `rivals`, AUTHORED ON 58 OF 66 FIGURES AND READ BY NOTHING SINCE SNG-208. 23 pairs are MUTUAL. ⚠️ A fight between rivals is not the same event as a fight between strangers, and the news must not report them in the same sentence.
   RIVALS      → name the rivalry. This is the fight people were waiting for.
   MUTUAL      → name it harder. Both of them have been waiting.
   STRANGERS   → say so. 'had not met before' is itself interesting.

strike._note: ⛔ SNG-596 / CCODE-364. A strike is a named sender going after a named target, and Erik's correction is the whole brief: 'don't just say came quietly — try to get the flavor of who was sent… was it an Umbral Assassin who used darkness, a radiant sniper, a marcher who tried a direct assault? how did they escape or win, did they have help, who and how?' ⛑ So every line here is built to carry {sWho} and {sHow} — who was sent and how they work — and to lose them cleanly in [brackets] when a minted figure has neither. ⛔ AND EVERY LINE MUST CARRY THE WORD 'strike', or 'came openly' for a crusade — §254 enforces it, and it is the point: the feed already carried landed strikes as ordinary duel lines, which is exactly why Erik could not find one.

killed: {T} is dead at {place}, and it was murder[ — {sWho}][, {sHow}]. No warning, and no witness who will say so.
A knife in the dark found {T} at {place}[ — {sWho}][, {sHow}]. No struggle, nothing taken[, and {S} has not been seen since].
{T} did not come back from {place}. Somebody was sent to kill them[, and it was {S}][, {sWho}][, {sHow}] — that is all anyone can put together.
wounded: An assassination attempt very nearly finished {T} at {place}[ — {sWho}][, {sHow}]. {t} is alive and is not walking yet.
{T} was ambushed at {place} by somebody who knew the work and meant to kill[ — {S}][, {sWho}][, {sHow}].
checked: Somebody came to kill {T} at {place}, got close enough to be sure of it, and went no further[ — {S}][, {sWho}][, {sHow}]. {s} did not stay to try twice.
There was an attempt on {T}'s life at {place}[. {S} made it][, {sWho}][, {sHow}]. It did not land.
stopped: Somebody was sent to kill {T} at {place} and was stopped short of them[ — {S}][, {sWho}][, {sHow}]. {t} did not have to lift a hand.
The attempt on {T}'s life at {place} was over before it was properly started[ — {S}][, {sWho}][, {sHow}].
stalemate: {S} came for {T} at {place} without a word between them, meaning to kill[, {sWho}][, {sHow}] — and both walked away from it.
Something happened to {T} at {place} and {t} will not discuss it. Somebody came to kill them[. {S} was there][, {sWho}][, {sHow}].
guarded: {T} was ambushed at {place}[ — {S}][, {sWho}][, {sHow}] — and {G} stood in the way[, {gWho}][, {gHow}][, with {gPower}]. {s} got away, but not unseen.
The knife meant for {T} at {place} found {G} first[. {S} sent it][, {sWho}][, {sHow}][ — {G} was {gWho}][, {gHow}]. Somebody in the valley knows the face.
{G} was between {S} and {T} at {place} when the knife came[, {gHow}][, with {gPower}], which was not an accident[. {s} is {sWho}][, {sHow}], and left without finishing the murder.
turned: An assassination attempt on {T} at {place} did not get there[. {S} was the hand][, {sWho}][, {sHow}]. Whoever stopped it has not said so.
Somebody came to kill {T} at {place} and failed[ — {sWho}][, {sHow}]. {t} is alive, somebody else is the reason, and neither is naming the other.

killed: {S} came openly for {T} at {place}[ — {sWho}][, {sHow}] — and {T} is dead. Nobody is pretending it was anything else.
{S} declared the strike and carried it. {T} fell at {place}[, {sWho}][, {sHow}], in front of enough people that the telling will be the same everywhere.
wounded: {S} came openly for {T} at {place}[, {sWho}][, {sHow}]. {t} lived. It was close, and everyone present saw how close.
{T} was put down at {place} by an open strike from {S}[, {sWho}][, {sHow}] and got back up. That is being talked about more than the attempt.
checked: {S} came openly for {T} at {place}[ — {sWho}][, {sHow}] and was turned back in front of witnesses. That costs something.
{S} made the strike on {T} at {place} in the open[, {sWho}][, {sHow}] and did not carry it.
stopped: {S} came openly for {T} at {place}[, {sWho}][, {sHow}] and was stopped before it was a fight. In the open, that is the expensive way to fail.
The declared strike on {T} at {place} ended early[ — {S}][, {sWho}][, {sHow}].
stalemate: {S} came openly for {T} at {place}[, {sWho}][, {sHow}] and they fought to nothing. Both are claiming it and neither is convincing.
The open strike on {T} at {place} ended where it started[ — {S}][, {sHow}]. The only thing settled is that it is not settled.
guarded: {S} came openly for {T} over {arc} at {place}[ — {sWho}][, {sHow}] — and {G} stood in the way[, {gWho}][, {gHow}][, with {gPower}].
{S} declared the strike on {T} at {place}[, {sWho}][, {sHow}] and got {G} instead[, {gHow}][, with {gPower}]. It was short and it was public.
Everyone at {place} saw {G} put themselves between {S} and {T} when the open strike came[ — {gHow}][. {s} is {sWho}][, {sHow}]. Nobody is sure yet what that costs {g}.

strike._intentWhy: ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-16: 'I didn't mean for you to use strike every time — I mean for the wording to be OBVIOUS that the intent was to kill you or the target. So assassination attempt, or a knife in the dark, or ambushed would all roughly do the same thing.' ⚠️ §254 TESTS FOR THE LITERAL WORD `strike` OR `came openly`, WHICH MADE EVERY LINE SAY IT THE SAME WAY — a correct gate testing too narrow a thing, which is the same shape as a hand-typed table standing in for a derived one. ⛑ THIS LIST IS THE GATE'S REAL SUBJECT: a strike line must make the INTENT unmistakable, and there are a dozen ways to do that. CCode: test membership of this list rather than one string, and it stays extensible as the prose grows.

_placeholders:
{W} full winner name (first mention) · {w} short winner · {L} full loser · {l} short loser · {place} location DISPLAY NAME, never an id · {power} the ability's short description.
⚠️ IF `place` IS NULL, DROP ' at {place}' RATHER THAN PRINTING 'at null'. If `power` is null use the non-`_power` variant. ⛔ NEVER PRINT A RAW ID — that is the 'the the_ceaseless' fault again.
⛑ SNG-596 STRIKE SLOTS: {S}{T}{G} sender/target/guard · {s}{t}{g} short forms · {sWho}{tWho}{gWho} 'a devourer of the Umbrals' · {sHow}{tHow}{gHow} the authored manner · {power}/{gPower} · {arc} lowercased mid-sentence. ⛔ [SQUARE BRACKETS] ARE DROPPED WHOLE when any slot inside them is empty — that is how a minted figure with no fighting style reads cleanly instead of trailing a comma.
_pick: ⛔ CHOOSE BY RELATIONSHIP FIRST, THEN POWER. If the two are mutual rivals use `mutual`; else if either lists the other use `rival`; else `stranger`. ⚠️ Use `_power` in place of the chosen variant roughly one time in three when an abilityId exists — the power should feel like a detail the teller happened to know, not a stat line on every entry.

fragments._note:
⛔ THE VERBLESS LINES, AND WHY ONE TEMPLATE COULD NOT FIX THEM. Testing revealed the fragments come in TWO GRAMMATICAL FORMS and my single template broke on the second:
   THIRD-PERSON VERB — 'pulls a novice back from dissolving', 'sells a secret that wasn't his'
   GERUND/NOUN — 'learning a faster road', 'a daughter who thinks he is a clerk'
⚠️ 'Overseer Grael WAS SEEN a daughter who thinks he is a clerk' is still not a sentence. ⛔ TWO TEMPLATES, CHOSEN BY THE FRAGMENT'S OWN SHAPE.

verbForm._when: the fragment begins with a third-person verb — ends in 's' on the first word, or is in `personalVerbs`
verbForm._example: 'The Hollow King of the Wild Half sells a secret that wasn't his.'

nounForm._when: the fragment is a gerund or a noun phrase — 'learning a faster road', 'a daughter who…'
nounForm._example: 'Sister Alder, the Ward That Does Not Break is spoken of: learning a faster road.' · 'Word from the Heights — Overseer Grael of the Edge District: a daughter who thinks he is a clerk.'

fragments._detect: ⚠️ CHEAP TEST: strip the leading article; if the first word ends in 's' and is not a known plural noun, treat it as a VERB form. Everything else is NOUN form. ⛔ WHEN IN DOUBT USE nounForm — '{W} is spoken of: {frag}' is grammatical for BOTH shapes, and a slightly stiff sentence beats a broken one.

_selection:
⛔ SNG-434. CCODE: '7 of 8 fights read they had never met — should rivals drive more fight selection?' YES, AND THE NUMBER SAYS SO OUTRIGHT.
   66 figures → 2145 possible pairings. 43 authored rival pairs. ⛔ A UNIFORM DRAW HITS A RIVALRY 2.0% OF THE TIME, so 85% of eight-fight ticks are ALL STRANGERS. The template is fine; THE SELECTION IS UNIFORM.
⚠️ PROPOSED WEIGHTING — rivals are not rarer, they are the POINT:
   MUTUAL rivals (34 pairs)  weight 12
   one-way rival (9 pairs)   weight 6
   same tradition            weight 2   — a schism reads as news
   strangers                 weight 1
⛔ THAT GIVES ROUGHLY 1 IN 3 FIGHTS AS A RIVALRY, not 1 in 50. ⚠️ AND DO NOT GO FURTHER: if every fight were a grudge the word would stop meaning anything, and 'they had never met' is a good line that deserves to land sometimes.
⚠️ SECOND CONSTRAINT: a mutual pair should not fire twice in a row. The stalemate/mutual line already says 'it is not the first time' — that only works if the engine KNOWS it is not.
_personalBeats:
⛔ CCODE: 'should personal beats draw from `offscreenVerbs`, the one field authored in the ACTIVE VOICE that this site does not read?' YES — AND IT IS THE FIELD I SHOULD HAVE POINTED AT WHEN I FIXED THE VERBLESS LINES.
   `offscreenVerbs` 66/66 · `personalVerbs` 66/66. ⚠️ THEY ARE DIFFERENT GRAMMARS AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ANSWER:
   offscreenVerbs — THIRD-PERSON ACTIVE: 'attends an ending unsent-for', 'builds another impossible thing', 'cuts a thread unasked'. ⛔ THESE DROP STRAIGHT INTO `{W} {frag}.` AND ARE SENTENCES.
   personalVerbs — noun phrases and gerunds: 'a daughter who thinks he is a clerk'. ⛔ THESE ARE WHAT BROKE, and they need `{W} is spoken of: {frag}.`
⚠️ SO PREFER `offscreenVerbs` FOR THE OFFSCREEN BEAT — it is authored for exactly this slot, it is already active-voice, and it needs no detector. Fall back to personalVerbs with the noun-form template.
⛔ THE VERBLESS BUG WAS A FIELD-CHOICE ERROR BEFORE IT WAS A GRAMMAR ERROR.
